beats.intent: ThinkSR keeps the super-resolution field dense while a compact DQ-CTM process updates it through shared recurrent ticks.
beats.claim: A persistent dense carrier, read and updated by a compact thought process.
beats.narration: ThinkSR starts by converting the low-resolution image into a dense carrier instead of asking the thought state to hold every pixel. The carrier is partitioned into windows so the compact process can work locally while the dense field stays present. The DQ-CTM thought process reads and updates the carrier over repeated ticks. Those ticks share parameters, so recurrence happens inside the thought stage rather than around the whole pipeline. The decoder turns the updated dense field back into the super-resolved output.

params.headline: ThinkSR runs dense features through compact recurrent thought
params.note: The loop belongs to the thought stage itself.

beats.intent: The carrier equation first makes a dense feature field from the low-resolution image, then partitions that field into windows without dropping tokens.
beats.narration: The equation defines the carrier that lets dense output coexist with compact thought. The encoder maps the low-resolution image into a dense feature field. The window partition operates on that field, keeping every token available to the following process.

beats.intent: DQ-CTM-SR is not the smallest model in the benchmark; at 1.129 million parameters, it is second largest among the five methods.
beats.narration: The parameter comparison should be read as a cost, not only as a result. CATANet is the smallest model in this table. RFDN and IMDN remain under one million parameters. DQ-CTM-SR uses 1.129 million parameters, making it the second largest of the five. CARN is larger still at 1.592 million parameters.
